data.narrative:
World Labs is a Series A artificial intelligence and software company founded by Fei-Fei Li, Ben Mildenhall, Christoph Lassner, and Justin Johnson, having raised $1.23B+ to date. The valuation analysis triangulates against a comparable universe of 4 primary peers in the AI & Software sector at same or adjacent stages (Scale AI, Reflection AI, Physical Intelligence, and Black Forest Labs), supplemented by a broader set of 9 private and 1 public reference companies.

Two valuation methods were applied. Stage-progression modeling, using total capital raised as a value proxy, implies a $2.5B valuation by applying a 2.0x multiplier typical of Series A advancement. Peer-median analysis across the 4-company comparable set yields $15.3B, reflecting the wide dispersion in this sector: the peer range spans $3.2B (Black Forest Labs, Series B) to $29.0B (Scale AI, Series B). The median peer is materially higher than the stage-progression result, likely reflecting strong recent fundraising multiples in frontier AI.

The triangulated analysis supports a valuation range of $2.1B (low) to $17.6B (high), with a median of $8.9B. The wide range reflects two primary uncertainties: (1) material stage and capital-efficiency differences among the peer set, and (2) the relatively early, pre-revenue status of the target, which limits comparable multiples on fundamentals. Weighting toward the lower half of the range may be appropriate pending clarity on differentiated product traction.
